# 1 Enoch Chapter 95 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch — Woe Oracles

---

**1** If only my eyes could become a raincloud — I would weep over you, I would pour out my tears like a downpour of rain. Maybe then the anguish in my heart would find some rest.

**2** Who gave you permission to practice contempt and wickedness? Know this: judgment is coming for you, sinners — it is already on its way.

**3** Don't be afraid of the sinners, you righteous ones. The Lord will hand them over to you again, so that you can bring judgment down on them — exactly as you desire.

**4** Woe to you who pronounce curses you cannot take back — healing will stay far from you, because of your sins.

**5** Woe to you who pay back your neighbor with evil — you will receive exactly what you have given.

**6** Woe to you, false witnesses, and to all who tip the scales toward injustice — you will perish suddenly, without warning.

**7** Woe to you, sinners — you who hunt the righteous. The time will come when you are hunted down yourself. You will be handed over, you will be persecuted, and the yoke of that injustice will crush you.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The raw emotion of v. 1 is extraordinary — the prophet-scribe weeps over the people he is condemning. This is not cold prophetic judgment; it is anguish. V. 3 then pivots to comfort the persecuted righteous. The woes of vv. 4–7 target specific social abuses: cursing with religious authority (v. 4), personal vendettas (v. 5), corrupt legal testimony (v. 6), and the persecution of the innocent (v. 7).*
